note: The tab list root. `width` fixes both previews at 600px, because the tab row's height follows its content and the two preview columns are different widths. The root is a text part: its height is driven by the tab labels, which are set in our own font. The focus state is left out of the state list, because it cannot be measured on either side. The reference stops the row clipping through `has-[:focus-visible]:overflow-visible`, and the census rewrites `:hover` and `:focus-visible` into attributes but not `:has(:focus-visible)` — so the reference's row can never be driven into that state and always reads `overflow: auto`. Ours implements the same behaviour through `data-focus-within`, set on the row by a focusin listener when the focused tab matches `:focus-visible`, with the generated rule `.tabs[data-focus-within] { overflow: visible }`. Verified by reading both. The behaviour belongs in the behaviour checks, not the style census.
